{"id":"mimid-1wgh.37.104","title":"wg: protocol-07 has no follower catch-up; design, spec, implement, then propose","description":"Mark, 2026-11-22: think it, design it, write a spec, deploy in mimid, then PR into other MIMI implementations. Arrived at from the opposite direction to meshIRCd's vector clock (bead ircd-fmu2 there).

THE GAP, verified in draft-ietf-mimi-protocol-07.txt. Application and handshake messages are submitted to the hub, which stamps an acceptance time and fans out to follower providers. Searching the draft for catch-up, missed, resync, backlog and fell-behind returns ZERO hits; retry appears twice and not for this. FanoutMessage carries the MLSMessage, an optional frank, a RatchetTreeOption and proposals, and nothing that identifies its position in the room's stream. The only ordering handle is accepted_timestamp in milliseconds, which is not an ordering key: two messages can share a millisecond and nothing promises monotonicity across a clock adjustment.

So a follower provider that is offline during fanout has no specified way to learn what it missed, and no way to ask. mimid papers over it with a push-only delivery queue on the hub; if the hub gives up or loses the queue, the follower's users lose messages and are not told. In MLS that loss can be permanent: the ciphertext only ever existed in that fanout.

IT WANTS A SCALAR SEQUENCE, NOT A VECTOR CLOCK. MIMI has exactly one writer per room, the hub, whose identity is baked into the roomId ('The hub of a room is the provider identified by the authority of the roomId'). Vector clocks reconcile concurrent origins, which MIMI forbids by construction. A monotonic per-room sequence assigned by the hub is sufficient and much cheaper to specify. Vector clocks return only for OPTIONAL follower-to-follower gap filling, and even there the hub's sequence stays authoritative: the question is who holds 400 to 450, not how to merge divergent histories.

DESIGN SKETCH, to be worked up in docs/design/mimi-catchup.md before any code:
1. A monotonic per-room sequence assigned by the hub, carried in fanout. Open question: a new FanoutMessage field is a wire change, so weigh it against the extension points of bead mimid-1wgh.55 and against carrying it beside the envelope rather than inside it.
2. A pull primitive, follower to hub: give me room R from sequence N. The response is the gap as FanoutMessages, in hub order.
3. Retention as the cost knob, and it must be stated: a hub keeps fanout for at least some window (mimid already has message_retention_secs, 7 days by default) and MUST answer explicitly when a request falls outside it, rather than returning a short answer that looks complete.
4. An unfillable gap must be visible all the way to the user. Silent loss is the thing being fixed, so a hub saying 'too old' has to surface as something the user sees. mimid has the pattern internally already: the store's feed answers TooOld and the front ends resync.
5. Authorization: only a provider that was entitled to the messages may fetch them, authenticated by the provider auth that already exists (RFC 9421 signatures, PKIX, DANE).
6. THE SUBTLE ONE, and the part most likely to be got wrong by an implementer: the hub MUST bound the response by the REQUESTER'S PARTICIPATION WINDOW. A provider that has left the room may backfill what it missed while it was a participant and must receive nothing from after it left. Otherwise catch-up becomes a retroactive read of a room you were removed from. Equally, a provider that joined at sequence 500 must not be handed 1 to 499.
7. Privacy note for the draft: a catch-up request tells the hub which rooms a provider follows and roughly when it was down.

ORDER OF WORK, deliberately implementation-first, per the reference-not-only rule and the chairs' standing request for implementation evidence:
a. the design note, for Mark's review;
b. implement in mimid, hub side (sequence, retention, the primitive, the participation-window bound) and follower side (notice the gap, ask, surface what cannot be filled);
c. only then propose: a WG issue against protocol-07 with the running code as evidence and proposed text, aiming for -08 rather than a separate extension draft, since the hole is in the WG's own document;
d. then offer it to other implementations. Haven is the realistic one: per the reference-not-only memory, only mimid and Haven speak protocol-07 on the wire. Every post needs Mark's per-action OK, and the peer-contributing-rules memory applies.

NOT PLANNED FURTHER: no sub-issues until Mark approves this plan.","status":"open","priority":2,"issue_type":"task","owner":"mark@reviewcommit.com","created_at":"2026-11-23T01:08:37.872889996Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","updated_at":"2026-11-23T01:08:37.872889996Z","labels":["wg"],"dependencies":[{"issue_id":"mimid-1wgh.37.104","depends_on_id":"mimid-1wgh.37","type":"parent-child","created_at":"2026-11-23T01:08:37.905009062Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","metadata":"{}"}]}

{"notes":"Design note written 2026-11-22: docs/design/mimi-catchup.md, 276 lines, for Mark's review. Sections: the gap as verified in protocol-07; why the room cannot be eventually consistent (RFC 9420's one Commit per epoch, no merge function, and the hub baked into the roomId); why a scalar sequence and not a vector clock; the sequence and the three placements for it; the catchUp primitive discovered through §5.1's directory templates; the unfillable-gap answer; retention as the stated cost; optional follower-to-follower filling; authorization and the participation-window MUST; privacy; what mimid implements on each side; Limitations; and four open questions for Mark.

The design's two load-bearing choices, both argued in the note:
- The primitive is DISCOVERED THROUGH THE DIRECTORY (a catchUp URI template beside notify, update, reportAbuse and proxyDownload). A provider that does not publish it does not support it, a requester learns that without a failed request, and no version negotiation is needed. That mechanism already exists and is how reportAbuse and proxyDownload were added.
- The sequence rides BESIDE the message in the notify envelope rather than inside FanoutMessage (recommendation; §4 gives all three readings). It keeps a parsed structure other implementations already handle stable, and the sequence is a property of the delivery rather than of the message.

The part most likely to be implemented wrongly, and which needs its own MUST in any proposed text: the hub bounds a catch-up answer by the REQUESTER'S participation window — nothing from before its first participant joined, nothing from after its last left. Otherwise catch-up is a retroactive read of a room you were removed from, a worse hole than the one being closed. The new state this needs is the mapping from participant-list changes to sequences, which the hub does not keep today.

Implementation sub-issues filed per Mark's instruction to bead it out."}
